industries.municipal.name: Municipal services
industries.municipal.lead: Grounds are large, there’s plenty of work and ever fewer people to do it. Leaf fall, snowfall and poplar fluff season aren’t getting any shorter.
industries.municipal.lead2: Robots take the long, repetitive passes along park paths, sidewalks and parking lots; people take work that needs hands and eyes. We choose equipment to fit how you buy.

Sweeping, surface washing, collecting leaves and poplar fluff. The robot covers long routes on a schedule; the crew handles bins, flower beds and anything that needs hands.
Interchangeable snow blades and brushes clear paths, squares and building entrances. One machine works all year round; only the attachments change.
We have not found production driverless snow removers in Russia yet: known projects are still in development.
Commercial robotic mowers are for level lawns in parks and courtyards. Slopes, dams and embankments call for remote-controlled equipment: the operator stands in a safe spot, not on the slope.
Koham and Leking: remote-control slope mowers with no autonomous mode.
Autonomous sweepers for open and indoor parking, squares and lots. Night cleaning works best, when there are fewer cars.
Pudu MT1: up to 1,800 m²/h in standard mode, 4–8 h of operation per charge.

industries.municipal.procurement.root.te: Areas, surfaces, seasonal work, and how you procure.
The buyer sets the OKPD2 code from the manufacturer’s documents.
If the robot falls under an item 98 code, a foreign machine can’t be bought.
So: a Russian manufacturer, or Route B.
The purchase covers grounds upkeep: areas, regulations, quality.
The contractor owns and services the robots and answers for the result.
Suits pilots and seasonal work: you pay for cleaned grounds, not for a machine.
industries.municipal.procurement.notes.l: This is not legal advice. The buyer decides which OKPD2 code (Russian product classification) a robot falls under, based on the manufacturer’s documents. Compact robots may fall under a different code. Check the current decree with a lawyer before buying. Names of Russian documents here are our own translations.
industries.municipal.procurement.notes.s: Sidewalks. The experimental legal regime for robots on sidewalks (Government Decree No. 1247 of 30 September 2026) targets delivery robots. Open sources don’t say whether it covers cleaning robots. In parks, the robot works on the customer’s own grounds.
